description: We are a group of students from different international schools around the netherlands, coming together to participate in NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are passionate about space, innovation, technology, science, and problem-solving, and we want to use our different skills and perspectives to create an innovative solution to a real-world challenge.
summary: Our project, "Abandoned but Not Forgotten," is a short animated educational video about NASA's space equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. Through an adventure featuring our team (Arya, Avika, Mahika, Ruchir, Daksh, and Steve), we explore forgotten rovers, scientific instruments, and spacecraft, explaining their missions, discoveries, and contributions to space exploration. Our goal is to make space history interesting and accessible while showing why these machines deserve to be remembered.
details:
Project: "NASA's Forgotten Space Equipment - Moon & Mars." It's a 4.5 min animated science film for kids, built in Remotion (React/TypeScript) - every frame is code, not edited footage. Six kid narrators in a zero-g "mission bus" broadcast take you through the Moon (Apollo descent stages, rovers, ALSEP, retroreflectors, the 96 waste bags) and Mars (Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity, water evidence, dust storm deaths, legacy). One storyboard file drives narration, animation, captions, and an SRT, so timing never drifts.

Benefits: accurate NASA facts, accessible captions, no stock footage or licensing issues, and fully reproducible - change one line and rebuild.

Impact: reframe "space junk" as heritage and show that dead rovers still underpin current missions.

Tools: TypeScript, React 19, Remotion, Node.js, SVG art, macOS say TTS, ffmpeg (loudness-normalized voice, synthesized music bed and SFX), h264/aac export at 1920x1080, 30 fps.

Creative: broadcast-style HUD, hand-built animated characters, original vector scenes instead of footage.

Considered: factual accuracy (dates, sols, counts), gentle tone about the dead rovers, caption readability and layout overlap, pacing, and a render crash fix for reproducibility.
projectRefs: Why is there poo on the moon?
